# Occasion and audience

## What this deck is made for

- Occasion: a training before the first risk assessment, or before a new round
- Audience: `practitioners`
- Length: 45 minutes, with a shared exercise at the end
- What the listeners already know: clauses 4 and 6 of ISO/IEC 27001 and the
  terms threat, vulnerability and residual risk

::: {.notes}
This slide is not presented. There is only this one deck for this topic. For
the leadership what is needed stands in the deck on ISO/IEC 27001, because its
decisions are the criteria and the approval and not the method.
:::

# What it is about

## The subject in one sentence

ISO/IEC 27005 carries the activity the controls come out of in the first place:
establishing what can go wrong, how heavily it would weigh, what comes first
and what happens to it.

## Why it concerns the practitioners

- ISO/IEC 27001:2022 requires in 6.1.2 and 6.1.3 that assessment and treatment
  happen, and leaves the how open
- This standard fills what is open, and it still prescribes no scale
- Anyone not settling the method settles it anew at every risk

# Four settlements before the first risk

## The four questions

- On which scale is the estimate made
- Above which value does treatment become obligatory
- Who may approve a residual risk
- Over what period is the thinking done

Without those four no later number is comparable, not even with itself next
year.

## How you notice they are missing

- Two people estimate the same risk differently and both are right
- No risk lies below the threshold
- Or every one does

# The run

## The order

- Settle the frame, so the four questions above
- Establish which risks there are
- Estimate how large they are, with a reason for every step
- Decide which have to be treated
- Treat: reduce, share, avoid or carry knowingly
- Have what is left approved
- Carry it on in operation rather than doing it once

## The step where it tips

- The controls follow from the treatment, and only afterwards comes the
  comparison against the annex of ISO/IEC 27001:2022
- Anyone taking the control collection first makes an inventory and not an
  assessment
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 6.1.3

## The silent mistake with several risks

- The resources do not run to all of those above the threshold
- Instead of writing the scarcity down, the third risk gets estimated lower
  until it falls below the threshold
- That is why the estimate stands before the decision about the order and not
  after it

# What gets written down

## Per risk

- The sentence saying what goes wrong and what is then lost
- Two steps with a reason each, not only the number
- The risk owner, so who answers for the consequences
- The chosen direction of treatment, with its reason
- The residual risk and its approval, with a date
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 8.2 and 8.3

## Including where nothing gets done

- A risk below the threshold gets carried knowingly and written down
- A missing line does not say whether nobody looked or whether nothing was
  there

# What to do or decide afterwards

## The next steps

- Write the four settlements down and have the leadership confirm them
- Take one first risk all the way through, with both reasons
- Set a point of return for the waiting risks, and hang it on an event and not
  only on a date
- Who, by when: belongs in the discussion and not on this slide

# References

## Standard, clause and edition

- ISO/IEC 27005:2022, as a whole standard
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 6.1.2, 6.1.3
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 8.2, 8.3
- ISO 31000:2018, as a whole standard

No text from a standard stands on these slides. No clause number of
ISO/IEC 27005 is named, and the reason stands in the chapter on that standard:
a number nobody has looked up looks checkable and is not.
